note: Hand-curated housing analysis of HB2, New Hampshire's omnibus budget policy trailer, for the 2021, 2023, and 2025 budget cycles. Candidates came from relevance-term matching over every extracted section (see working/.../hb2/{year}/); a human pass kept the housing sections and logged every exclusion. Roll-call votes are recorded on HB2 AS A WHOLE - a vote for or against the trailer is never a vote on one section, and must not be presented as one.

relevant_sections.heading: Department of Health and Human Services; Bureau of Adult and Elderly Services; Congregate Housing and Services
relevant_sections.plain_language: Suspended the state's congregate housing and congregate services programs for older adults (Medicaid waiver services) for the 2022-2023 budget years - a service cut, not an expansion.

relevant_sections.heading: New Section; Commission to Study Limiting the Business Tax Credit Carry Over
relevant_sections.plain_language: Created a study commission on business tax credit carry-overs that was told to examine letting companies put unused credit refunds into affordable housing development.

relevant_sections.heading: New Subdivision; Department of Business and Economic Affairs; Office of Planning and Development
relevant_sections.plain_language: Created the Office of Planning and Development inside the Department of Business and Economic Affairs - the state office that helps cities and towns with land use planning and housing data.

relevant_sections.heading: Electric Renewable Portfolio Standard; Renewable Energy Fund
relevant_sections.plain_language: Directed part of the state's renewable energy fund toward community solar projects that serve manufactured-housing communities and multi-family rental housing.

relevant_sections.heading: Appropriation; Affordable Housing Fund
relevant_sections.plain_language: Put $25 million into the state's Affordable Housing Fund (run by New Hampshire Housing) to finance or match funding for affordable housing projects.

relevant_sections.heading: Appropriation; Department of Health and Human Services; Transitional Housing Beds
relevant_sections.plain_language: Put $6 million into transitional housing beds - raising the rates paid for the beds and funding new ones for patients leaving New Hampshire Hospital and people with complex behavioral health needs.

relevant_sections.heading: New Subdivision; InvestNH Program
relevant_sections.plain_language: Wrote the InvestNH fund and program into law - a standing fund that makes grants and loans to speed up municipal approvals and support housing construction. (InvestNH began in 2022 with federal money; this made it permanent in statute.)

relevant_sections.heading: Appropriation; InvestNH
relevant_sections.plain_language: Put $10 million into the InvestNH fund for its municipal-approval and housing-construction grants.

relevant_sections.heading: Appropriation; Affordable Housing Fund
relevant_sections.plain_language: Put another $25 million into the Affordable Housing Fund, non-lapsing, for financing or matching funds for affordable housing.

relevant_sections.heading: Congregate Housing; Appropriation
relevant_sections.plain_language: Restored $1.5 million for the congregate housing and congregate services programs for older adults that the 2021 budget had suspended.

relevant_sections.heading: Appropriation; Department of Health and Human Services; Targeted Medicaid Rate Increases
relevant_sections.plain_language: Within a package of Medicaid rate increases, raised the housing reimbursement rates paid on behalf of people receiving community mental health services.

relevant_sections.heading: Board of Manufactured Housing; Repeals
relevant_sections.plain_language: Repealed the Board of Manufactured Housing (RSA 205-A:25-31) effective September 1, 2023 - the state board where manufactured-home park residents and park owners could resolve disputes without going to court. A separate bill to restructure the board (SB203) died between the chambers the same year.

relevant_sections.heading: New Section; Superior Court; Land Use Review Docket
relevant_sections.plain_language: Created a land use review docket in the superior court - a dedicated court track for appeals of local planning and zoning decisions, intended to speed up housing-related land disputes.

relevant_sections.heading: New Subdivision; New Hampshire Housing Champion Designation and Grant Program
relevant_sections.plain_language: Created the New Hampshire Housing Champion program: cities and towns that volunteer to adopt housing-friendly regulations, train land boards, and invest in water/sewer capacity earn a designation that unlocks state grants. This enacted the substance of SB145, which had passed the Senate 21-3 as a standalone bill.

relevant_sections.heading: Positions Established
relevant_sections.plain_language: Created the state staff positions to run the Housing Champion program.

relevant_sections.heading: Application of Receipts; Dedicated Funds
relevant_sections.plain_language: Set up the dedicated-fund accounting so Housing Champion money stays in its own fund.

relevant_sections.heading: Appropriations; Housing Champion Designation and Grant Program Fund
relevant_sections.plain_language: Funded the Housing Champion program: $5 million for the grant fund plus $250,000 for administration.

relevant_sections.heading: Appropriation; Department of Health and Human Services; Transitional Housing Beds
relevant_sections.plain_language: Extended the 2021 budget's $6 million transitional-housing-beds appropriation so it would not expire until mid-2025.

relevant_sections.heading: Department of Health and Human Services; Homeless and Housing Shelter Programs; Appropriations
relevant_sections.plain_language: Put $8 million into raising the rates the state pays homeless shelter programs, plus $2 million for shelter assistance including cold-weather shelter and hotel placements.

relevant_sections.heading: Housing Finance Authority; Study on Graduated Public Assistance Mandated
relevant_sections.plain_language: Ordered New Hampshire Housing to study a graduated, proportional rental assistance voucher for people who do not qualify for existing programs, reporting by November 2023.

relevant_sections.heading: Department of Business and Economic Affairs; Division of Planning and Community Development Established
relevant_sections.plain_language: Reorganized the state planning office into a Division of Planning and Community Development that administers the state's planning, broadband, and housing programs.

relevant_sections.heading: Department of Health and Human Services; State Grant in Aid
relevant_sections.plain_language: Directed $5 million a year for two years from the opioid abatement trust fund to year-round emergency shelter for people with opioid use disorder, with services aimed at recovery and permanent housing.

relevant_sections.heading: Congregate Housing; Appropriation
relevant_sections.plain_language: Funded congregate housing and congregate services for older adults at $350,000 a year for two years.

relevant_sections.heading: New Section; Partners in Housing Program
relevant_sections.plain_language: Created the Partners in Housing program: state funding for workforce housing built on city-, town-, or county-owned land that is transferred to developers, with at least 20 percent of units meeting workforce-housing rules.

relevant_sections.heading: New Paragraphs; Power to Review Site Plans
relevant_sections.plain_language: Let municipalities fast-track site plan review for residential projects on state-listed surplus properties, and let solely residential workforce-housing projects use the quicker 'minor site plan review' where a town has adopted it.

relevant_sections.heading: Housing Champion Designation and Grant Program Fund; Compilation of Property
relevant_sections.plain_language: Extended the Housing Champion fund's purpose to also pay for compiling the list of municipal and county property suitable for residential development.

relevant_sections.heading: Board Established
relevant_sections.plain_language: Shrank the Housing Appeals Board - the state board that hears appeals of local zoning and planning decisions - from 3 members to 2.

relevant_sections.heading: New Section; Administrative Attachment
relevant_sections.plain_language: Attached the Housing Appeals Board to the Board of Tax and Land Appeals for budget and administration, with shared staff.

relevant_sections.heading: Appointment; Term; Chair
relevant_sections.plain_language: Changed Housing Appeals Board members from fixed terms to serving 'at the pleasure of' the governor and Executive Council, who also pick the chair.

relevant_sections.heading: New Section; Tie Vote; Resolution
relevant_sections.plain_language: Set a tie-breaker rule for the now 2-member Housing Appeals Board: a member of the Board of Tax and Land Appeals casts the deciding vote.

relevant_sections.heading: Board of Tax and Land Appeals; Quorum
relevant_sections.plain_language: Adjusted the Board of Tax and Land Appeals quorum rules to fit its new role backing up the Housing Appeals Board.

relevant_sections.heading: Appropriations; Housing Champion Designation and Grant Program Fund; Lapse Extension
relevant_sections.plain_language: Extended the 2023 Housing Champion appropriation ($5 million) so it would not lapse until mid-2026.

relevant_sections.heading: Appropriation; Department of Health and Human Services; Supportive Housing Services
relevant_sections.plain_language: Ordered the state to renew and fully implement a Medicaid benefit paying for supportive housing services, with progress reports to the legislature in 2025 and 2026.
